title: Buy the engine and axle donors now, before the freeze?
ask: Should the engine and rear-axle donors be bought now from today's yards (about $430), before the design freeze, while the CD009 still waits on the clearance proof?
options:
(a) Buy the engine and axle donors now, from today's sightings - the LM4 if it is still there, otherwise the freshest LC9 - plus a V8 Explorer's 8.8. About $430 plus cores at U-Pull-&-Pay's posted prices ($250.99 engine without accessories, $180.99 disc rear end), and a day's trip. They are measured for the CAD. The CD009 (about $1,650-2,150 shipped) still waits on the clearance proof (CD06). Forecloses nothing: the parts are cheap and resellable.
(b) Find and track only (D-626 as it stands). Re-run the search before each decision; buy after the freeze. Costs nothing now. The LM4 will almost certainly be gone, and the CAD is built from figures until then.
(c) Buy all three now, the CD009 included. The CAD is exact soonest, but about $2,100-2,600 is spent before any clearance is proven.
recommend: (a), unless you want no money spent at all before the freeze - then (b).
stops: BR02 (the engine pull), BR07 (the axle), and when the CAD becomes exact (CD08's measurements).

title: Swap: as planned, a running F-body donor, or a different car
ask: Should the FB get the swap as planned (a), the drivetrain of one running LS1 / T56 Camaro or Firebird (b), be sold for a car that is already what you want (c), or wait while the other projects finish (d)?
why:
Camden, 2026-10-16: "then this begs the question is the swap with it, i am roughly 6k into the car as of now. is there a car i could find for a reasonable price that would be a good starting point for my optimized perfected design that i could get for less then that? then i just have to rework some of the ends of the wireing project and the space and everything changes but a lot transitions over without needed to remanufacture the whole car for 30k"

What the swap costs, from the record's parts and options plus estimates for what is not priced yet:
- Everything except the engine (gearbox and adapter, ECU, fuel, axle, drive, cooling, clutch, exhaust, tune) is about $14,000-26,000.
- With the engine, a running car is about $17,000-32,000 (junkyard restore, D-628) to $24,000-38,000 (new crate).
- DS10 computes the real figure once the design prices everything.

What the market says (2026-10-16 searches):
- Finished LS-swapped RX-7s sell for far less than they cost to build. A dated forum estimate puts LS FCs at $7-12k and LS FDs at $15-25k; no FB sale was found.
- A 1998-2002 Camaro / Firebird LS1 books at about $4,400-8,700 (KBB). The 6-speed T56 cars ask more.

Why a running F-body donor is the middle path:
- One car brings a tested, running LS1 and a T56 that bolts to it with no adapter. This replaces the CD009 ($1,650-2,150) and the Sikky kit ($1,765).
- It also brings the F-body oil pan (DS02's first candidate), the low F-body drive with A/C, the clutch hydraulics and the pedal.
- The shell, seats, wheels and 10-bolt axle sell to win back about $1,000-2,500.
- It still needs the FB tunnel checked for the T56: an FB LS3 / T56 build did it (OP11). It also needs a 160 A alternator (D-457).

What moves to another car if the FB is sold: the PMU and the crimper (already bought), the EMU PRO plan, the CAN dash design, and the method. Everything built on the FB itself does not move: the harness legs, cavity maps, box mounting, the factory-circuit work, the luxury parts and the SA CAD model. That half of the electrical project would start again.

The $6,000 already spent is gone either way; only the money still to spend decides this. Market figures are estimates to confirm with live listings before anything is bought.
options:
(a) Keep the swap as planned (D-628): a junkyard aluminum 5.3, the CD009 on the Sikky adapter. About $17,000-32,000 to a running car. Every design choice stays open and the result is the lightest, best-packaged FB. The most money and the most time.
(b) Keep the FB but take the drivetrain from one running 1998-2002 Camaro / Firebird LS1 6-speed. About $5,000-8,000 for the car, less $1,000-2,500 from selling what is left; about $12,000-24,000 to a running car, roughly $4,000-8,000 under (a). Heard running before it is pulled, the T56 needs no adapter, and the F-body pan and drive suit the FB. Costs: the LS1 is iron-sleeved aluminum like the 5.3 but higher-mileage, the T56 tunnel fit is to prove, and the CD009 plan, D-628's donor and parts of the engine rows are reworked.
(c) Sell the FB as it stands and buy a car that is already what you want: an LS-swapped FC or FB, or a clean RWD manual car such as a 350Z, an E46 330Ci (the six) or an LS1 F-body, for about $7,000-15,000. Driving soonest and cheapest. The FB, its 6,000 already in it and the FB-specific half of the electrical, luxury and CAD work are left behind.
(d) Pause the engine and finish the car's other projects first (electrical, luxury), deciding the drivetrain later. No engine money now. The car does not run until it is decided, and the electrical project's engine end waits.
recommend: (b), unless driving soon at the least cost matters more than this FB - then (c)
stops: Buying anything for the engine (block 01.65, J5, SR01, SR03, SR04) and the engine-side design that depends on the gearbox (CD03, J4, DS07). The car's other projects go on
